decisions.reason: Its dedicated page suggests relatively strong strategic commitment, and with only one year of market exposure management would likely use organisational slack to keep learning rather than exit quickly.
As an adjacent apron-operations module, it is close enough to the firm's digital complement strategy that early ambiguous results would probably still clear a modest exploratory aspiration level.

Revenue calculation and billing is the weakest fit with an electrical-equipment firm's core capabilities and, being only lightly presented, would be a likely target for problemistic resource reallocation if early results disappointed.
Equipment monitoring software fits closely with the firm's installed-base and engineering strengths, so management would be inclined to retain it while demand information is still forming.
Apron resource management is somewhat more peripheral than monitoring but still part of a coherent airport software offering, making continued trial more likely than immediate withdrawal.

The controller safety alert service is strategically attractive but niche and only lightly signalled on the website, so it carries elevated risk yet would still more likely be kept for another year of evaluation.
